name: Congenital Horner Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Horner Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of unilateral mild ptosis due to paralysis of the superior tarsal muscle
Ipsilateral pupillary miosis with preserved light reflex
Ipsilateral facial anhidrosis or decreased sweating
Iris heterochromia on the affected side (lighter iris color)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of unilateral ptosis and miosis with or without anhidrosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical; pharmacologic testing and imaging may assist in confirming diagnosis and ruling out acquired causes.

imaging: MRI or CT imaging of the brain, neck, and chest to exclude acquired causes
Pharmacologic testing with apraclonidine or cocaine eye drops to confirm sympathetic denervation
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; often sporadic or associated with birth trauma
other: Clinical observation of anisocoria and ptosis

distinguishingFeatures: Possible associated pain or neurological deficits
Potential underlying mass lesion or trauma
Different pattern of extraocular muscle involvement

redFlags: Sudden onset of Horner syndrome in older children or adults
